title: Homework should be abolished in schools
context: Whether take-home assignments help or harm learning and wellbeing.
for_points: excess homework increases stress and cuts into sleep
learning gains from homework are small for younger students
time at home is better spent on reading, play, and family
against_points: homework builds independent study habits early
practice outside class consolidates what was taught
it shows parents what their children are learning

title: School uniforms should be mandatory
for_points: uniforms reduce visible income differences between students
they cut daily distraction and peer pressure over clothing
a shared identity improves school belonging
against_points: uniforms suppress self-expression during formative years
they add a recurring cost for low-income families
there is little hard evidence they improve results

title: Online learning is as effective as classroom learning
context: The post-pandemic debate on digital education.
for_points: online courses let students learn at their own pace
they open access to top teachers regardless of location
recorded lessons can be reviewed as often as needed
against_points: classrooms build social skills that screens cannot
the digital divide leaves poorer students behind
motivation and attention drop without in-person structure

title: Board exams should be replaced by continuous assessment
context: One high-stakes test versus year-round evaluation.
for_points: a single exam rewards memorisation over understanding
continuous assessment reduces one-day pressure and anxiety
it gives teachers early signals to help struggling students
against_points: standard exams are the fairest common benchmark
continuous marks are easier to inflate or bias
students learn to perform under pressure, a real-world skill

title: AI tools should be allowed in classrooms
context: Tools like chatbots as tutors or as shortcuts.
for_points: AI tutors give every student personalised help
students must learn to use the tools they will use at work
teachers save time on routine marking and planning
against_points: AI makes it easy to skip the thinking that builds skill
it produces confident but wrong answers students cannot detect
it widens the gap between those with and without access

title: Social media should be banned for under-16s
context: Child safety and mental health versus access and freedom.
for_points: heavy social media use is linked to teenage anxiety
algorithms are designed to maximise compulsive use
children cannot meaningfully consent to data collection
against_points: bans are easily bypassed and push teens to riskier platforms
social media connects isolated young people to support
education and parental tools work better than prohibition

title: Remote work is better than office work
for_points: remote work removes hours of commuting each week
it widens hiring beyond one city
many studies show stable or higher individual productivity
against_points: spontaneous collaboration and mentoring suffer at a distance
young employees lose the learning that happens in person
the boundary between work and home blurs into burnout

title: Governments should be allowed to access encrypted messages
for_points: criminals and terrorists hide planning behind encryption
lawful access with warrants keeps oversight in place
platforms already scan for some illegal content
against_points: a backdoor for governments is a backdoor for hackers
mass access chills free speech and journalism
determined criminals will simply switch to other tools

title: Single-use plastics should be banned completely
for_points: single-use plastic is a major source of ocean pollution
alternatives already exist for most everyday uses
bans change habits faster than voluntary campaigns
against_points: some plastics are vital for hygiene and medical safety
alternatives can have higher carbon footprints
better waste management solves the problem at the source

title: Nuclear energy is the answer to climate change
context: Low-carbon baseload power versus risk and cost.
for_points: nuclear provides reliable, near-zero-carbon baseload power
it uses very little land per unit of energy
modern reactor designs are far safer than older ones
against_points: new plants take over a decade and huge budgets to build
long-term waste storage is still unresolved
solar and wind are now cheaper and faster to deploy

title: Every country should adopt a carbon tax
for_points: a carbon price makes polluters pay the true cost
it rewards clean innovation without picking winners
revenue can be returned to households as a dividend
against_points: carbon taxes hit low-income households hardest
industries simply relocate to countries without the tax
developing nations should not pay for emissions they did not cause

title: Meat should be taxed to protect the environment
for_points: livestock is a major source of methane and deforestation
a tax nudges diets without banning anything
revenue can fund sustainable farming
against_points: a meat tax is regressive and hits poorer families
diet is a cultural and personal choice
farm efficiency improvements cut emissions without new taxes

title: The voting age should be lowered to 16
for_points: 16-year-olds pay taxes and live with long-term policy effects
voting early builds a lifelong habit of participation
young people are well informed through school and media
against_points: most 16-year-olds are still developing independent judgement
they are more easily influenced by parents and teachers
other adult rights begin at 18 for good reason

title: Voting should be compulsory
context: Turnout and legitimacy versus freedom of choice.
for_points: compulsory voting makes results reflect the whole population
it reduces the influence of extreme, motivated minorities
it works in countries such as Australia
against_points: the freedom to vote includes the freedom not to
forced voters may cast random or uninformed ballots
governments should earn turnout, not mandate it

title: The UN Security Council veto should be abolished
context: Reforming the five permanent members’ power.
for_points: the veto lets one country block action on atrocities
the 1945 power structure no longer reflects the world
abolition would restore the Council’s credibility
against_points: the veto keeps major powers inside the UN system
without it, powers may ignore the Council entirely
reform should expand membership rather than remove the veto

title: All elected leaders should face strict term limits
for_points: term limits stop leaders entrenching personal power
they bring fresh ideas into government
they reduce long-term corruption networks
against_points: term limits remove experienced, effective leaders
voters, not rules, should decide who governs
lame-duck leaders lose accountability in their final term

title: Governments should provide a universal basic income
context: A guaranteed income in an age of automation.
for_points: UBI is a safety net as automation replaces jobs
it removes bureaucracy from targeted welfare
pilots show recipients invest in education and work
against_points: UBI is extremely expensive at national scale
it may reduce the incentive to work
targeted support helps the poorest more per rupee spent

title: A four-day work week should be standard
for_points: trials show productivity holds while wellbeing rises
it reduces burnout and sick leave
it can spread work and cut commuting emissions
against_points: many services cannot simply close for a day
small businesses face higher costs to keep cover
compressed hours can raise daily stress

title: Extreme wealth should be taxed far more heavily
for_points: extreme inequality concentrates political influence
wealth taxes can fund health and education
much of top wealth grows untaxed as unrealised gains
against_points: wealth taxes are hard to value and easy to avoid
capital and founders may leave the country
several European countries scrapped them as ineffective

title: Cryptocurrency does more harm than good
context: Financial innovation versus speculation and crime.
for_points: crypto markets are dominated by speculation and scams
mining consumes large amounts of energy
anonymity helps fraud, ransomware, and money laundering
against_points: crypto gives the unbanked access to financial services
blockchain enables transparent, programmable payments
regulation, not rejection, can address the risks

title: Zoos should be banned
for_points: captivity causes stress and abnormal behaviour in many species
animals exist for entertainment rather than their own welfare
documentaries and sanctuaries can educate instead
against_points: accredited zoos run vital breeding programmes
they fund field conservation and research
seeing animals in person builds public support for protection

title: Celebrities have a duty to be role models
for_points: celebrities shape the values of millions of young fans
influence that is paid for comes with responsibility
positive role models change behaviour at scale
against_points: fame does not oblige anyone to model a lifestyle
parents and teachers are the right role models
expecting perfection leads to hypocrisy and backlash

title: Space exploration is a waste of money
context: Priorities on Earth versus investment in the future.
for_points: funds are urgently needed for poverty and health on Earth
private companies can fund space themselves
returns from crewed missions are uncertain
against_points: space research produced GPS, weather forecasting, and medical tech
satellites are essential for climate monitoring
exploration inspires students into science careers

title: The death penalty should be abolished worldwide
for_points: wrongful convictions cannot be undone after execution
evidence for deterrence is weak
it is applied unequally across class and race
against_points: some crimes are so severe that only the highest penalty is just
it gives closure to victims’ families
nations should decide their own criminal justice
